reasoning: Test plans and detailed test cases or scripts are distinct artifacts produced at different levels of detail. Y separates them without splitting the alternative forms of detailed test design unnecessarily.

X recasts ongoing monitoring as individual defect-status updates without assuming every follow-up involves retesting. Y adds a periodic reporting activity and assigns it a substantial share that the target does not establish.

The target is participation in product design reviews, with the listed topics describing the input provided. X codes that interaction directly; Y assumes a separate written-comment deliverable not specified by the task.
Specifying quality standards and developing procedures for assessing against them produce meaningfully different deliverables. Y distinguishes the criteria from the methods used to apply them.

Installation, maintenance, and use of testing software are distinct activities with different outputs. X covers maintenance changes and repairs as well as upgrades, whereas Y narrows maintenance to upgrades.

Feedback can be delivered as a written artifact or through discussion with developers, and these have different work products. X distinguishes those activities rather than treating all communicated feedback as a discrete deliverable.

X turns monitoring into an actionable performance issue without presuming a separate periodic report. Y assigns a substantial share to reporting even though the target does not establish that output or its frequency.

Coordination can involve organizing testing, communicating during the round, and handling its results, not just arranging it beforehand. X covers more of that coordination than Y, although its shares and the extent of reporting will vary by workplace.

Traveling to a beta site does not make software evaluation hands-on physical work. Y treats the visit and its findings as one evaluation rather than assuming a separate report is always written afterwards.
